sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Tantra** (*tantra*) ​— The ‌Loom of ‌Esoteric Doctrine ​· A ​class of ​works teaching ​magical and ​mystical formularies, ‌mostly cast ​as dialogues ​between Śiva ‌and Durgā ​— belongs ‌to the ​Sanskrit tradition, where ‌it is ​catalogued under ​the domain ​"Weaving, Esoteric ​System". The ​name means ‌"A class ​of works ‌teaching magical ​and mystical ‌formularies, mostly ​cast as ‌dialogues between ​Śiva and Durgā; ‌hence the ​esoteric systems ​of doctrine ‌and ritual ‌founded upon ‌them."[^1].

**Tantra** ​is the ​name of ‌a scripture-class ​and the ​ritual systems ‌those scriptures ​teach: works ​cast as ‌dialogues between Śiva ​and the ‌Goddess, embracing ​mantra, mandala, ​initiation, and ​the disciplined ​transgression of ‌ordinary purity-rules. ‌From the ​sixth-century Śaiva ‌scriptures to ​Tibetan Vajrayāna, ​the tantras ‌are the ‌Indian religions’ ‌most ambitious technology ‌for accelerated ​transformation.[^2]

PuniCodex ‌records the ​canonical scholarly ​spelling **Tantra** ​and serves ‌its temple ​at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/tantra/). The ​displayed form ‌is ASCII-equivalent ​— a ​description computed ​from the displayed ‌form itself. ​The plain ‌ASCII form ​*tantra* contains ‌the same ​letters: no ‌recovered diacritics ‌or special ​encoding is ​claimed. The ​work here ​is consistent ‌citation, capitalization, ‌provenance, and ​cultural context[^3].

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, transliteration, canonical spelling, name variations, and evidence preservation.
sections.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in Devanagari ​as ​**तन्त्र**. Etymologically ​it ​means "A ​class ‌of works ​teaching ​magical and ‌mystical formularies, ​mostly ‌cast as ​dialogues ‌between Śiva ​and ​Durgā; hence ​the ​esoteric systems ​of ‌doctrine and ​ritual ‌founded upon ​them."[^1].

‌The canonical ​spelling ‌**Tantra** matches ​the ‌conventional scholarly ​romanization. ​The plain ‌ASCII form ‌*tantra* ‌contains the ​same ​letters, so ‌no ​lost diacritics ​or ‌encoding transition ​is ​claimed. The ‌editorial ​work is ‌to ​fix one ​reviewed ​reference spelling, ​preserve ‌capitalization and ‌provenance, ​and keep ‌the ​original evidence ​visible. The ‌displayed ‌form is ‌ASCII-equivalent ‌— a ​description ‌computed from ​the ​displayed form ​itself.

‌The letter-by-letter ​transformation ​runs:

- **t** ​→ ‌**T** — ​Same, ​capitalized
- **a** ​→ ‌**a** — ​Same
- ‌**n** → ​**n** — ‌Same
- ​**t** → ‌**t** ‌— Same
- ​**r** ​→ **r** ​— ​Same
- **a** ‌→ ‌**a** — ​Same

sections.label: Pronunciation
sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is **/ˈtʌntrə/** ​— ​Sanskrit ​(IAST: Tantra).[^1]

‌Phoneme ​by ​phoneme:

- **Tan-** ‌— ​From ‌√tan, “to ​stretch, ‌extend, ​weave” — ​the ​same ​root as ​“tan” ‌and ​“tend”.
- **-tra** ‌— ​The ‌instrumental suffix: ​the ‌tantra ​is the ‌“loom” ​or ​“warp” — ‌the ‌extended ‌doctrine.
- **** ​— ​The ‌word names ​both ​the ‌scripture-class and ​the ​ritual ‌systems those ​scriptures ‌teach.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ​the closest ‌approximation ‌is: ​“TUN-truh”

Kindred ‌and ​historical ​forms of ‌the ‌name:

- ‌**Root** — ‌√tan ​— ‌to stretch; ​English ​“tend”, ​“tension” are ‌cousins
- ​**Etymology** ​— tantra ​— ‌the ​warp of ​a ​loom, ‌the system’s ​threads

‌The ​word is ‌a ​weaving-metaphor: ‌the tantra ‌is ​the ​warp into ​which ​the ‌practice’s threads ‌are ​stretched.

sections.body:
**Tantra** ​is the ‌name ‌of a ​scripture-class ​and the ​ritual ​systems those ​scriptures ‌teach: works ​cast ​as dialogues ‌between Śiva ​and ‌the Goddess, ​embracing ‌mantra, mandala, ​initiation, ​and the ​disciplined ​transgression of ​ordinary ‌purity-rules. From ​the ‌sixth-century Śaiva ​scriptures ‌to Tibetan ​Vajrayāna, ‌the tantras ​are ‌the Indian ​religions’ ​most ambitious ‌technology for ‌accelerated ‌transformation.[^1]

### The ​Scripture-Dialogue

​The tantra ‌is ​cast as ​Śiva’s ‌answer to ​the ​Goddess’s questions ‌— ​god and ‌power, ​doctrine and ​energy, ​in conversation.

### ​The ‌Maṇḍala

The ‌deity’s ​palace-diagram, constructed ‌from ​coloured sands ​or drawn, ‌entered ‌by initiation ‌through ‌the four ​gates.

### ‌Mantra and ​Mudrā

​Sound and ​gesture: ‌the mantra ​pronounced, ​the hand-seal ​struck ‌— the ​body ​made instrument ​of ‌the doctrine.

### ​Transgression ‌as Method

​The pañcamakāra ‌— ​the five ‌M’s ‌— consumed ​in ​ritual under ​vow, ​inverting purity ‌to ‌burn through ​it.

sections.label: Symbols
sections.body:
The ​iconography ‌associated ‌with Tantra ​concentrates ​in ​a ​small ​set of ‌recurring ​attributes, ​each ‌a ​compressed ‌statement about ​the ‌name:[^1]

- ​**The ​Scripture-Dialogue** ​— The ​tantra ​is ‌cast ​as ‌Śiva’s ​answer to ‌the ​Goddess’s ‌questions ​— ‌god and ​power, ​doctrine ‌and ‌energy, ‌in ​conversation.
- **The ​Maṇḍala** ‌— ​The ​deity’s ‌palace-diagram, constructed ​from ​coloured ‌sands ​or ‌drawn, ​entered by ​initiation ​through ​the ‌four ‌gates.
- **Mantra ​and ‌Mudrā** ​— ​Sound ‌and ‌gesture: the ‌mantra ‌pronounced, ​the ‌hand-seal ​struck — ​the ​body ‌made ​instrument ​of ​the doctrine.
- ‌**Transgression ​as ​Method** ​— ‌The pañcamakāra ​— ‌the ​five ‌M’s ​— ‌consumed in ‌ritual ​under ​vow, ​inverting ​purity to ‌burn ‌through ​it.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
Tantra’s mythology ​is its own ‌theology of secrecy ‌and speed: the ​god teaching the Goddess, ​the guru initiating ​the disciple, and ​the householder’s body ​becoming the ritual ‌ground. Its stories ​are the scriptures’ ​frames — Śiva ‌on Mount Kailāsa ​answering Pārvatī’s midnight questions, ‌the siddhas flying ​on mantra-power, the ‌kings protected by ​Śaiva rites.[^1]

### The ​God Teaches the ​Goddess (Tantric Frame)

​Nearly every tantra ​opens on a ‌mountain: Śiva, asked by ​the Goddess how ‌liberation may be ​quick for the ‌poor in merit ​and short in ‌life, answers with ​the system. The ‌gender of the ​exchange is the doctrine ​— the god ‌is knowledge, the ‌Goddess is energy, ‌and the tantra ​is their union ​written down for ‌the age of ​decline.[^2]

### The Clan-Traditions ​(Kaula & Śaiva Cycles)

‌The early Śaiva ​tantras organised themselves ​as kulas, clans ‌— initiatory lineages ​bound to a ‌deity, a mantra, ​and a guru. ​The clans’ mythology made ​heroes of the ​siddhas, the perfected ‌ones who flew, ‌stayed young, and ​turned the elements ‌— the tantras’ ​advertisements and their ​cautionary tales.

### The ‌Thunderbolt Vehicle (Vajrayāna Cycle)

‌Buddhism absorbed the ‌tantras wholesale: the ‌Vajrayāna made the ​Buddha speak as ‌Vajradhara, the thunderbolt-holder, ​and taught that ​buddhahood could be ​won in a ‌single lifetime. The Tibetan ​canons — Kanjur ​and Tanjur — ​are the largest ‌single body of ​tantric scripture preserved ​anywhere.

### The State ​of the Rites ‌(Royal Protections)

Medieval ​kings ruled by tantra: ‌the Śaiva rites ​of protection (rakṣā) ‌and the pacificatory ​rites (śānti) were ‌statecraft. The inscriptions ‌of the Cōḻas ​and the Pālas ​record land-grants to ​tantric monasteries that anchored ​their realms — ‌the esoteric schools ‌as the polity’s ​immune system.
